# Exact obstruction to an alternating-sector area-product bound

Use K={(x,y):x>=0,y>=0,x+y<=3}, with centroid g=(1,1). Let
C_0={x+y<=2}, C_1={x>=1}, C_2={y>=1}; let D_ij=K intersect C_i
intersect C_j, and let E_i be the part of K in C_i alone, disregarding
null boundaries.

The proposed homogeneous auxiliary inequality

    product_i |Q intersect E_i|
       <=8 product_{i<j}|Q intersect D_ij|

is false, even for a triangle Q that contains g in its interior.
Take

    Q=conv{(0,0),(3,0),(9/10,6/5)}.

It lies in K and g has barycentric coefficients (1/12,1/12,5/6) in Q,
so all required incidences are strict. Exact polygon clipping gives

    (|Q intersect E_0|,|Q intersect E_1|,|Q intersect E_2|)
       =(5/8,5/8,1/70),

    (|Q intersect D_01|,|Q intersect D_02|,|Q intersect D_12|)
       =(1/2,1/56,1/56).

The ratio of these two products is 35, strictly larger than eight.
These values are computed using only rational segment intersections and
the shoelace area formula in
`../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_triangle_cone_product_obstruction.py`.

For clarity, the more modest fixed-cap signed-area assertion is not
refuted here. In fact

    |Q intersect E_i|-2 sum_{j!=i}|Q intersect D_ij|
       =(-23/56,-23/56,-2/35)

for i=0,1,2, respectively. Each of the three candidate signed caps
therefore satisfies the desired nonpositive inequality in this example.

A parameterized version is
Q_epsilon=conv{(0,0),(3,0),(1-epsilon,1+2epsilon)}. Its centroid g is
interior for every epsilon>0. For 0<epsilon<=1 it lies in K. The same
exact verifier checks epsilon=1/2,1/10,1/100, with product ratios
245/27,35,3283/2. The single rational example above suffices to disprove
the proposed universal constant eight; no numerical optimization enters
the certificate.
